newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Zim offers fixed day service.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Zim offers fixed day service.

text.p: Zim Israel Navigation Ltd said on Tuesday it was initiating a fixed-day weekly service on the Asia-Israel-Adriatic line (Asia-Med).
The company said in a statement that the service would be fully operational by the end of July.
It said the increased frequency of service was made possible by the addition of a tenth vessel to the line.

"The line's round trip will be shortened, the line will turn in Korea and the weekly service to Japan will be given by transshipment via Pusan or alternatively by ZCS via the Panama Canal, at the customer's choice," it said.
"Israeli trade to and from Adriatic ports and Alexandria will be on a weekly fixed-day basis by the Asia-Med line."

The service will operate through Israel's Haifa port but Zim said customers could receive cargo in Ashdod or use a "'combined bill of lading' service bringing cargo to the customer's door under preferred terms".
Zim posted a first quarter loss of $12.8 million on Monday. It attributed the loss to the continuing decline of freight rates.
Zim is 51 percent controlled by the Israel Corp, with the remaining owned by the Israeli government.
